elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: § 12.4 ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor") is deleted in full

elements.element: No field-of-use / territory restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: remaining § 12.3: "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... or conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: no restriction remains; "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no ... non-compete ... commitment"
the term-plus-24-month clause was removed rather than narrowed
"for twenty-four months thereafter" deleted, not replaced with a 12-month cap
no carve-out language inserted; only offered in the non-operative comment
no carve-out language inserted; only offered in the non-operative comment

reasons: The locked target is preferred, and deleting § 12.4 in its entirety achieves exactly that: no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer remains, and § 12.3's affirmative acknowledgement is now internally consistent.

Minimality is satisfied notwithstanding the automated gate: the deleted paragraph consisted solely of the offending non-compete covenant, so there were no unrelated words or mechanics within it that could have been preserved by a narrower edit; no substitute or boilerplate text was added.
Intent is preserved: § 12.3 and all other commercial terms remain untouched and effective, and no cross-reference, defined term, or dangling mechanic is created by removing § 12.4.

Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) are not present in operative text, but that is irrelevant because the preferred level is fully met and the two levels must not be blended.
